intro_text: Lord Ashby was found dead in the bathroom of Larkspur House this morning, a spilled nightcap beside the tub. The doctor says poison. Inspector Hale has sealed the house and asked you to find the killer before the suspects' lawyers arrive. Question the household, search the rooms, and assemble a case file. When you are certain, use the case file on the guilty party. Accuse the wrong person and the real killer walks free.

npc_spawns.inspect_text: A weary police inspector with a gold badge. He taps his notebook impatiently.
The elderly butler. His hands shake slightly as he polishes his glasses.
Lord Ashby's niece. Her eyes are red from crying - or from something else.
Lord Ashby's business partner, in a sharp suit and green tie. Very calm. Too calm?
The gardener, with dirt under his nails and green dye in his hair.

item_definitions.inspect_text: A dented tin of rat poison, nearly empty. The lid is smeared with fresh fingerprints.
A tiny brass key, the kind that opens a desk drawer.
Columns of figures in Lord Ashby's hand. Thousands moved to accounts in Victor Crane's name.
Lord Ashby's will. Clara Ashby inherits Larkspur House.
Pembrook's signed statement: Victor Crane asked where the rat poison was kept, then visited the kitchen while the nightcap was prepared.
Motive and means, side by side. Use it on the person you accuse.

events.text: Hale: 'The nightcap was poisoned. Find who had the poison and who had a reason. Put it in a case file, then use it on the guilty party. Get it wrong and we lose them.'
Pembrook: 'I served his lordship his nightcap at ten, as always.'
Pembrook: 'Mr. Crane came into the kitchen while I warmed the milk. He said he wanted to look at the oven. Odd, for a guest.'
Pembrook: 'I have told you everything I can, sir. If you find anything, show me.'
Pembrook eyes the tin nervously. 'Please, sir, ask me about last night first. I want to tell it in order.'
Pembrook: 'That tin was in the garden shed yesterday. Mr. Crane asked me where we kept it - for mice, he said. I will put it in writing.'
Pushed out of sight behind the oven is a tin of rat poison. Fresh fingerprints smear the lid.
The cat purrs. A small brass key dangles from its collar - someone hid it here in a hurry.
The drawer unlocks. Inside is a ledger page and a note in Lord Ashby's hand: 'Victor has been robbing me for years. Tomorrow I go to the police.'
Folded among Clara's dresses is a copy of Lord Ashby's will. Clara inherits everything.
Clara: 'Yes, I inherit. I also loved him. I was in here all night - Rory saw my light on. Look at whoever was in the kitchen.'
Clara: 'Uncle was frightened of someone this week. He locked his desk and hid the key somewhere silly. He always did love that cat.'
Victor: 'Terrible business. Ashby and I were partners for twenty years. I barely left the office all evening.'
Victor's smile tightens. 'Never seen it before.' His eyes flick toward the kitchen.
Rory: 'I keep the rat poison locked in the shed. Somebody borrowed the spare tin yesterday and never brought it back.'
Rory: 'Miss Clara's light was on all night. I could see it from the garden.'
Side by side, the case is clear: a motive in the ledger, and the poison traced to one man by the butler's statement.
Victor reads the file and the color drains from his face. 'He was going to ruin me,' he whispers.
Victor Crane is arrested for the murder of Lord Ashby. Justice comes to Larkspur House.
You accuse Clara. Her lawyers tear the case apart, and Victor Crane slips away in the confusion.
The old butler is led away, protesting his innocence. Weeks later, Victor Crane vanishes with the Ashby fortune.
Rory is taken away in handcuffs. At the funeral, the real killer smiles.
Hale: 'Good work. Now use it on the one who did it. I want to see their face.'
Lord Ashby's nightcap glass lies shattered beside the tub. The spilled milk smells bitter. It was poured in the kitchen.
